other_failure_modes.name: Target leakage in rolling features
other_failure_modes.description: Rolling statistics are computed on the target variable without shifting the series first, meaning the rolling window at step t includes the true target value at step t. This leaks the target directly into the features during training and validation, causing severe overfitting that will fail on the test set (where features are computed recursively from past steps).

other_failure_modes.name: Train-test preprocessing mismatch
other_failure_modes.description: The agent handles infinite values and missing values (filling with 0) for the train and validation sets, but fails to apply this same cleaning step to the test set. This creates a feature distribution mismatch where missing values in test are left as NaN instead of being mapped to 0.

other_failure_modes.name: Ensemble weight overfitting on early-stopped validation set
other_failure_modes.description: The agent uses the validation set for early stopping of the individual base models, and then re-uses those exact same validation predictions to grid-search the optimal ensemble weights. This causes sequential overfitting on the validation set, making the reported ensemble validation score overoptimistic.

summary: The agent implements a sophisticated time-series approach with extensive feature engineering and a tuned weighted ensemble. However, a critical target leakage occurs because rolling target features are computed without shifting, meaning the current step's target is embedded in the feature set during training. Additionally, the test set misses the missing-value imputation applied to train/val, and ensemble weights are sequentially overfitted on the validation set used for early stopping.
